messages.author: 5840f43b00eb4381
messages.subject: INLA nested hierarchical model translation
parts:
Hi,

I need some help converting a nested hierarchical LME4 model to the INLA format. This is the model as I would enter it in LME4:
deaths = intercept + year + (1 + year | state / zip_code)

I've been struggling with converting the (1 + year | state / zip_code) into the INLA f(.) format. I don't know how to specify the state, zipcode and year so that the zipcode is nested in the state and that the effect of year varies by state/zipcode.

So far, I think this is the correct formulation. Since I expect there is correlation between state and zip_code random effects, I'm using "iid2d":

formula <- deaths ~ 1 + f(ID, model = "iid2d", n =  145800 ) + f(unit, year, copy = "ID")
n = 145800 b/c I have 72900 entries
ID = 1:72900 (I think this is the ID for state)
unit = 1:72900 (I think this is the ID for the zipcode)
year = continuous variable

Is the INLA formulation equivalent to the LME4 formulation? If not, how would I specify this in INLA? Is "iid2d' the correct correlation model?

Thanks!


Best,
Jamie
